title: Fractures, Sprains & Dislocations
summary: Support the injured part in the position found, stop any bleeding, and apply a wrapped cold pack. Do not try to straighten it.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for serious limb injuries
when: Bone visible or wound over the fracture (open fracture)
Limb is deformed, cold, pale or blue, or has no feeling beyond the injury
Suspected fracture of the thigh, hip or pelvis, or several injuries
Suspected head, neck or back injury

steps.title: Check for danger and other injuries
steps.text: Do not move them unless necessary. Check for head, neck or back injuries and for severe bleeding first.

steps.title: Control bleeding from open fractures
steps.text: Cover the wound with a clean dressing. Apply pressure around – not on – any protruding bone.

steps.title: Support the injury
steps.text: Keep the limb still in the position you found it. Support it with padding, cushions or the person's own hands. Splint only if you are trained and need to move them.

steps.title: Cold pack for sprains and closed injuries
steps.text: Apply a cold pack or ice wrapped in a cloth for up to 20 minutes at a time.

steps.title: Check circulation
steps.text: Check beyond the injury for colour, warmth and feeling. Loosen bandages if fingers or toes become cold, pale, blue or numb.

steps.title: Get medical help
steps.text: Arrange transport to hospital or call {EMERGENCY}. Watch for signs of shock.

warningSigns: Cold, pale or blue skin beyond the injury
doNot: Do not try to straighten a deformed limb or push bone back in
Do not put ice directly on the skin
Do not let them eat or drink if they may need surgery

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
sources.title: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid
International Consensus on CPR and ECC Science With Treatment Recommendations (CoSTR)

review.notes: Drafted from the cited guidelines. Must be checked by a qualified clinician against the current editions and local protocols before operational use.
